title: The swing
hookLine: Kabir's swing holds every world; the cowherd girls want a God with a face
tomorrow: Kabir went out looking for a bad man. who did he find?

lines: THE MIND HAS MADE A SWING.
cards: Zoe has gone back and forth all week: push Theo to go to the wedding, or leave it alone. Back, forth. Kabir has a song for that motion, and it's bigger than one week.
In Tagore's English: "Between the poles of the conscious and the unconscious, there has the mind made a swing: Thereon hang all beings and all worlds, and that swing never ceases its sway."
Everything that exists, rocking on one swing. Elsewhere Kabir sings a God beyond every form; here, even the Lord takes form to ride it.

teach.b: Whether God has a form at all is an old argument in India, and it has a story. In the Bhagavata Purana, Krishna has left the village of Braj, and the gopis, the cowherd women who love him, are heartbroken.
He sends his wise friend Uddhava with a message: I'm not really gone; I'm the formless Self in all things; meditate on that. The gopis listen, and they answer back.

teach.h: WE HAD ONE MIND. IT WENT WITH KRISHNA.
teach.b: In the songs of the poet Surdas, they tell Uddhava: we had one mind, and it went with Krishna. We don't have a second one for your formless God. Give us the dark boy with the flute.
Here are both sides at their best.

teach.h: NIRGUN: NO FORM CAN HOLD GOD.
teach.b: Kabir's side, called nirgun: God has no form, so no picture can hold God, and no image can shut anyone out.
The gopis' side, called sagun: love needs a face. You can't hold the hand of an idea, and God, out of love, takes a form we can love back.
That's why, in the rainy season, some temples and homes hang a swing for Krishna, called Jhulan, and rock his image gently on it.
Hindu devotion kept both ways side by side: Kabir's swing of all worlds, sung by a poet of the formless, and the little swing with a face on it.

how: Hindu devotion honors both nirgun bhakti (love for God beyond form, as Kabir sang) and sagun bhakti (love for God with form, as in Krishna and Ram); in the rainy season, Krishna temples hold Jhulan, rocking his image on a decorated swing.

o: Kabir's picture of all worlds swaying between two poles
a rope bridge pilgrims cross on the way to a shrine
a playground ride Kabir used to teach children

games.q: two sides of the swing: tap the pairs.
p: brings a message about the formless Self
we had one mind; it went with Krishna
God without form; no image can hold God
God with form; love needs a face

s: Hindu devotion settled on one side: God either has form or doesn't
it kept both: nirgun bhakti and sagun bhakti, side by side.
in Surdas's songs, the gopis politely accept Uddhava's formless teaching
they answer back: their one mind went with Krishna, and they want him.
Kabir's swing holds all beings and all worlds
'thereon hang all beings and all worlds, and that swing never ceases its sway.'

games.q: you're on Kabir's side, God beyond form. a friend asks for the gopis' best case. what's the strongest thing they'd say?
o: images are just art, so they don't really matter
love needs a face; God takes a form so we can love back
the formless God is too hard, so faces are for beginners
games.why: that's the sagun case at its best: you can't hold the hand of an idea, and God, out of love, takes a form.

practice: Sit where you can move a little, and rock slowly forward and back, the way a swing slows down. Let each sway get smaller. When you come to rest in the middle, stay there, and feel the stillness that was under the swaying all along.

wordCard.voice: The swing: Kabir's picture of every world rocking between two poles, and Krishna's swing at Jhulan. Two ways of loving God, one motion.

orig.note: Hindi: swing. At Jhulan, in the rainy season, Krishna's image is rocked on one.

carryVoice: Carry this: the swing. Hindu devotion holds both the formless and the face. See you tomorrow.
